title: Services
description: A small service catalogue: who owns a service, how critical it is, where it lives in your CMDB, and what in Steward belongs to it.
name: Name
ownersHelp: Users and teams who may edit this service: user:<name> or team:<name>
archiveConfirm: Archive {{name}}? It disappears from the list and the link picker; links and history stay.

emptyState.title: No services yet
emptyState.text: Your administrators or designers add the services your team runs.
emptyState.textCreate: Add the services your team runs and link their platforms, monitors and records.

documents.title: Documentation
documents.linkNote: The document links to {{name}}. The editor opens next.
documents.noType: There is no record type for living documents. An administrator can add one under Records → Record types.
documents.empty: No documents for this service yet.

statusPages.title: Status pages
statusPages.description: Read-only pages for colleagues outside the service team: how the chosen services are doing, planned and running maintenance, known issues with vendors and – if you want – the availability objectives. They name no monitors, platforms or tickets.
statusPages.emptyText: A status page shows a few services for stakeholders, e.g. the plant colleagues: built from the monitors linked to the services, the maintenance windows and open vendor tickets.
statusPages.linkOnce: Anyone with this link sees the page without signing in. It is shown only now – copy it. A new link replaces this one; revoking ends it.
statusPages.servicesHelp: The state of a service comes from the monitors linked to it (service → links).
statusPages.showVendorIssues: Show known issues with vendors (the vendor and since when – never the ticket)
statusPages.noticeHelp: Shown at the top of the page, e.g. what you are doing about a problem.
statusPages.linkInvalid: This status page link is not valid (any more). Ask the person who sent it to you.
